runs.title: What happened with the Marine Osprey in Bladen County?
runs.prompt: On the morning of 8 October 2026, a US military aircraft caught fire and made an emergency landing in Bladen Lakes State Forest, Bladen County, North Carolina. Start at this local news article from WECT and report the verified facts: the aircraft type, how many people were aboard, their injuries, and the full statement from the Marine Corps spokesperson. Stick to what officials and named sources say.
runs.answer: Per WECT (Oct. 8, 2026): The aircraft was an MV-22B Osprey based out of Marine Corps Air Station New River, belonging to Marine Medium Tiltrotor Squadron (VMM) 162; it caught fire during military training and made an emergency landing in the Bladen Lakes State Forest area. Four Marines were aboard. White Lake Fire Chief Dale Brennan said one was taken to a burn center for injuries, while the other three were uninjured and flown back to base; NCIS is leading the investigation. The Marine Corps spokesperson's full statement (from 1st Lt. Cailin Altonen, 2nd Marine Aircraft Wing): "At approximately 10:20 a.m. EDT on Oct. 8, 2026, an aviation mishap occurred involving an MV-22B Osprey belonging to Marine Medium Tiltrotor Squadron (VMM) 162 near Bladen County, North Carolina. Four personnel were aboard the aircraft and are receiving medical care. Civilian and military emergency services responded to the site. The MV-22B Osprey was based out of Marine Corps Air Station New River. This incident is currently under investigation."

runs.answer: At the Rolex Shanghai Masters, French world No. 99 Terence Atmane (24) faced Bernard Tomic in the first round of qualifying; frustrated by an unforced error early in the deciding set, he smashed his racket against the court and the net, then flung it toward the terraces where fans were gathered. The racket struck the metal barrier/railing at the top of the court wall and did NOT hit anyone — the barrier was the only thing stopping it from clattering into a spectator (reports say it missed the front row by inches). He was not defaulted; the chair umpire gave him a code violation for unsportsmanlike conduct and a point penalty, and he then retired in the third set at 6-3, 4-6, 5-3 (a game from the finish). His reason/explanation, given in an Instagram Stories apology, was stress: being ranked inside the top 40 (peaked No. 41 in April) and then dropping to almost outside the top 100 (No. 99) made him "way more stressed and pressured than I could possibly imagine"; he added it did not excuse his behavior and that he would take a step back to "rebuild myself from zero," citing "health issues (not mental but actual health)."
